title: David and Jonathan (Avot 5:16)
hook: love that depends on something ends; love that doesn't, like David and Jonathan's, never does
tomorrow: is it bold, or just rude, to ask the director for a favor?

segments.voice: Yesterday, four students: sponge, funnel, strainer, sieve. Keep the fine flour. Today, a harder kind of keeping: keeping a friend.

Graduation season scatters people. Different cities, different time zones, one last group photo, and everyone promises to stay close. Some friendships make it; some quietly don't. So does a friendship survive the distance? Avot doesn't measure miles. It asks what the love was resting on. And then it picks two examples so strange they need solving.
screen: `ONE LAST GROUP PHOTO.` → `DOES IT SURVIVE THE DISTANCE?` → `WHAT WAS IT RESTING ON?`

segments.voice: Avot 5:16: any love that depends on a thing, when the thing is gone, the love is gone. Love that doesn't depend on a thing never ends. Which love depended on a thing? Amnon and Tamar. Which didn't? David and Jonathan. Here's the puzzle. Amnon and Tamar isn't a romance. It's one of the hardest stories in the Bible, and a gentle warning if young ears are listening. Amnon, a son of King David, wanted his half-sister Tamar, and harmed her. Then, the book of Samuel says, his hatred for her was greater than the love he'd had. Avot's point is grim and exact: what he called love was wanting. Once he'd taken the thing, nothing was left. And David and Jonathan? Jonathan is King Saul's son, the heir. David is the one who will take the throne that should have been his. If Jonathan's love rested on anything, a crown, a benefit, it would have broken. Instead Samuel says Jonathan loved David as his own soul. They're parted. Jonathan dies in battle. And Avot calls theirs the love that never ends. So distance isn't the test, and neither is death. The test is what it rests on. A friendship built on sharing a hallway ends with the hallway. One built on each other doesn't.
screen: `WHEN THE THING IS GONE.` · `AMNON: WANTING, NOT LOVE.` · `JONATHAN: NO CROWN NEEDED.` · `THE TEST IS WHAT IT RESTS ON.` · then, large: `LOVE WITHOUT CONDITIONS.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and bring one person to mind. For a few breaths, set aside everything they do for you: the rides, the help, the laughs, the use. Notice what's left when all of that is put down, and stay with it.
screen: `ONE PERSON.` · `SET ASIDE WHAT THEY DO FOR YOU.` · `WHAT'S LEFT?`

segments.voice: David and Jonathan: Avot's picture of love that depends on nothing. Parted, and still the love that never ends.
A line for the people you'll miss: love without conditions doesn't end with the hallway. Talk soon.

howItsDone: Jewish tradition holds up David and Jonathan as the model of friendship; Avot 5:16 is read with chapter five on summer Shabbat afternoons, and some teachers pair it with 1 Samuel 18 and 20.

fork.reveal: Avot's test isn't distance. David and Jonathan were parted for good; their love didn't depend on a thing, so it didn't end.
